settings.label: Chains
settings.why: empty takes every chain in the file

settings.label: Hotspots
settings.why: residue numbers of this structure, as 54,56,66-70 or A54,B12-16. Needed by the cards that aim at a site - the design tools and ADCP, and HADDOCK docking when it docks by the interface. A folded structure is numbered by the sequence it was folded from, so 54 is its 54th residue and the chains are named from A

cards.name: Boltz-2
cards.tagline: fold a sequence, or co-fold a complex
cards.note: One sequence folds one structure, for a target card to take. Fill in a second sequence and the two are folded together as a complex - a receptor with the DNA, RNA or peptide that binds it - which goes on to be prepared and simulated. A structure of more chains than three is a job for the Boltz-2 page.

settings.label: Sequence
settings.why: one chain, in one-letter codes. Case does not matter - neither tool makes the distinction, so a sequence pasted in lower case is read as upper - but a letter that is not a residue does, and is refused here rather than folded as nothing

settings.label: What it is
settings.why: the alphabet the sequence is checked against, and the model used for it

settings.label: Copies
settings.why: more than one folds a homo-oligomer: the same sequence again as chains A, B, C

settings.label: Sequence of the second chain
settings.why: fill this in to fold a complex rather than one chain: the two are folded together, in the order of the boxes, and what comes out is a complex

settings.label: What the second one is
settings.why: the alphabet it is checked against, and the model used for it

settings.label: Sequence of the third chain
settings.why: fill this in to fold a complex rather than one chain: the two are folded together, in the order of the boxes, and what comes out is a complex

settings.label: What the third one is
settings.why: the alphabet it is checked against, and the model used for it

settings.label: Alignments
settings.why: fetch asks the alignment server for one per protein chain while the flow is being queued, on the login node, which is the only place that can reach it. single folds from the sequence alone: nothing is fetched, and the structure is markedly worse

settings.label: Structures to fold
settings.why: each is a separate sample of the same model, and five takes about five times as long. They are handed on best first, and the card below takes the best few of them

settings.label: Recycling steps
settings.why: Boltz-2's own default. More costs time roughly in proportion

settings.label: Card
settings.why: auto takes the largest card this cluster has. A card the cluster has not got is refused before anything is queued

settings.label: Walltime
settings.why: importing the tool takes the first five minutes of it. A job that ends early is charged for what it used, so round up rather than cut it fine

cards.name: HADDOCK docking
cards.tagline: dock proteins, DNA or RNA onto the target, by its interface
cards.note: Takes the target as the receptor and each folded structure as a partner.

notes.auto: protein-DNA or protein-RNA when a partner is DNA or RNA, protein-protein otherwise
notes.protein-RNA: the same nucleic acid settings, for RNA

settings.label: Drive the docking by the target's hotspots
settings.why: the hotspots named on the target card become the receptor's active residues, and each partner's whole surface is passive; untick to dock ab initio

settings.label: Partners' chains
settings.why: as A,B; empty docks the whole of what was folded
settings.placeholder: every protein, DNA and RNA chain folded

notes.quick: 200 rigid-body models, 40 refined: for checking a flow
notes.standard: 1000 rigid-body models, 200 refined: HADDOCK's own default
notes.thorough: 2000 rigid-body models, 400 refined: for ab initio docking

settings.label: Complexes to hand on
settings.why: per partner: the best model of each of its best clusters. What leaves this card is then ranked across all of its partners together, best score first

settings.label: Walltime
settings.why: left empty, the docking works one out from the size of the molecules and the sampling

cards.name: Prepare
cards.tagline: prepare the receptor and the partner each on its own, then rejoin them
cards.note: Put in by the canvas on every link that carries a structure into a docking card or the simulation, and part of that link rather than a card of its own: it splits what arrives into the receptor and the partner, prepares each on its own - protonation at the pH above, termini, disulfides, gaps - puts them back together and checks the net charge. A side of several chains is prepared whole, so the bonds between its chains are kept. Into a docking card the waters and hetero groups are dropped, except the ions that docking can use. What it decided is listed on the card when it has run.

settings.label: pH
settings.why: every molecule is protonated at this pH, and one flow has one pH

notes.propka: pdb2pqr with propka at the pH above: each titratable residue gets the state its own surroundings call for
notes.pdbfixer: PDBFixer's rules at the pH above, which are the standard states and no more
notes.none: the hydrogens in the file, or the engine's own defaults where there are none

settings.label: Longest gap to model, residues
settings.why: a gap inside a chain up to this long, found from the sequence the file records, is built, relaxed and its joins checked, as ADCP builds one; a longer one is left open and its two ends capped (Cap the breaks). 12 at most, 0 builds none, and a chain's missing ends are never built

settings.label: Crystal waters
settings.why: for the simulation; into a docking card every water is dropped

notes.far: keep those within 5 Å of the partner

settings.label: Keep metals and cofactors
settings.why: into the simulation they ride through at their own coordinates, and it decides which side of the interface each belongs to; into a docking card only the ions that docking can use are kept, and the rest are listed as dropped

settings.label: Cap the breaks
settings.why: a gap left open has its two ends capped, an NME on the residue before it and an ACE on the residue after it, so neither is a charged terminus the protein does not have; the chain's own termini stay charged. Off, each piece ends in charged termini, an OXT before the gap and NH3+ after it

settings.label: Minimise each molecule
settings.why: restrained, in vacuum: it takes the clashes out and moves nothing else

settings.label: Walltime
settings.why: one job prepares everything that arrives, a few minutes a molecule

cards.name: Prepare receptor
cards.tagline: prepare the target's receptor once, for the docking
cards.note: Put in by the canvas between a target and every docking card it feeds, once per target: the target's chains alone, through HOPE-MD's Prepare - protonation at the flow's pH, AMBER names, termini and breaks, gaps up to the length above built back from the sequence the file records - with the waters and hetero groups dropped, except the ions the docking can use. The hotspots are checked against what comes out: one on a built residue is flagged on the card, and one that is missing stops the docking, by name.

settings.label: pH
settings.why: the receptor is protonated at this pH, and one flow has one pH

notes.propka: pdb2pqr with propka at the pH above: each titratable residue gets the state its own surroundings call for
notes.pdbfixer: PDBFixer's rules at the pH above, which are the standard states and no more
notes.none: the hydrogens in the file, or the engine's own defaults where there are none

settings.label: Which of what arrives to simulate

settings.label: Settings for one structure
settings.why: a group per structure, as name: key=value, key=value, with a semicolon between groups. The keys are this card's own, so "3cc1_cluster2: length_ns=200, engine=openmm" runs that one structure for longer on another engine and leaves the rest alone
